svg.text: S1 GRAB FROM TOP — stacked boxes, one trolley above them
Lidded boxes stand directly on each other in 9 stacks. A trolley in the roof lifts any top box and puts it on any stack.
126 box positions GN 1/6-100, 113 usable · 194 per metre of wall
3 motors (2 CoreXY + 1 hoist), 0 in the gripper
top box ≈ 4–5 s · mean ≈ 6 s · worst 72 s · est. €1,100–1,400 + grid €600
Front and side views: lighter boxes = taller stacks behind.
orange = trolley (moves in X and Y)
THE BOXES (one footprint, any height on any other)
• GN 1/6, flange 176 × 162 mm, flat lid 10 mm on top
• hooks grip the flange underside at the middle of the
two 162 mm sides (they run in the 12 mm gaps)
• nothing may stick out of the flange outline
• RFID tag in a flange corner, ≤ 5 kg

g.text: 1/7 The trolley waits over A-R. The box for tonight was moved to the top of stack C-F during the night.
2/7 Two belt motors (CoreXY) move the trolley over stack C-F.
3/7 The gripper plate goes down on two steel tapes and lands on the lid of the top box.
4/7 Touch-down: the slack tapes flip a cam, the hooks swing under the box flange. No motor in the gripper.
5/7 Up to the dock: the load cell weighs the box, the RFID tag is read.
6/7 Over to the port stack B-F under the roof hatch: set down, hooks open, plate up, trolley leaves.
7/7 The roof hatch opens; the K9b gallery hoist lifts the box out and carries it to the cooking cell.
A box on top takes ≈ 4–5 s. A buried box is dug out first: see S1-retrieval.
